The ORB broke UP through 10559.2 but current price (10585) is already above the overnight high (10577.1); the next structural ceiling is the prior day high at 10616.2, just 31 points away — a natural profit-taking magnet that could stall longs.

briefing.briefing: Starting with the currency picture — GBPUSD is up +0.13% today and sitting at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range, meaning sterling is unusually strong right now. Because UK100 and GBP move in opposite directions (a stronger pound makes FTSE's big dollar-earning companies like Shell, HSBC and Unilever worth less in pound terms), this is a quiet but persistent drag on the index, even though the overall macro picture looks broadly positive. On the sector front, the picture is split: miners (Rio Tinto, Glencore) are a tailwind today with copper up +1.05% — copper is watched as a gauge of global economic health — but energy heavyweights Shell and BP face pressure from Brent crude falling -1.64%, which partially offsets that gain. Banks are roughly flat given gilt yields [the interest rate the UK government pays on its borrowings] nudging up just 2 basis points — no stress there, with the long-end gilt stress flag firmly off. The main headline from the past 12 hours (roughly 12 hours ago) is an intensifying US-Iran conflict, which has pushed the broader risk mood slightly negative, though markets are so far shrugging this off — US equities are up 0.6% and the Nasdaq is up 1.18%, keeping a helpful floor under sentiment. AstraZeneca remains a wildcard — as the largest single stock in the FTSE 100 by weight, any stock-specific news today could override everything else discussed here. Directional bias leans mildly BULLISH — the ORB [Opening Range Breakout, the price range set in the first few minutes after the London market opens at 08:00] has already broken upward, European markets (DAX +0.52%, Euro Stoxx +0.49%) are aligned, and US futures are firm. However, confidence is only 5/10: the strong pound is a cap on gains, 58% of the typical daily range (which averages 132.8 points over the last 14 days) has already been used with the index at 10585, leaving only around 56 points of typical room to the upside before the market runs out of its usual daily energy — that limits how far any breakout can travel. What would change this view: a reversal in GBP (a sudden pound drop would be bullish for FTSE), a deterioration in the US-Iran situation escalating to genuine risk-off selling, or an AstraZeneca-specific headline. For the 08:00 ORB trade specifically, the upside break has already printed and is technically supported by the macro backdrop, but the combination of a strong pound and 58% of the daily range already consumed suggests this is more likely a grind than a clean trending day — trail stops [automatic exit orders that move with the price to lock in profit] tightly on any long. On the calendar, there is no high-impact data scheduled for today, but tomorrow at 07:00 BST brings the UK Labour Market Report (employment and wage data — HIGH impact, just one hour before the ORB window), followed by UK CPI inflation data on Wednesday at 07:00 BST — both capable of sharply moving sterling and the index, so position sizing into tomorrow's open deserves extra caution. Key levels: ORB high is 10559.2, ORB low is 10512.5, overnight high 10577.1, with the prior day high at 10616.2 acting as the next meaningful ceiling — current price at 10585 is already above the overnight high, so bulls need to clear and hold 10616 to confirm momentum.
